output.title: Expedited Prior Authorization Decision Timeframe
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does an expedited prior authorization decision take?

A: When a prior authorization request qualifies for expedited (urgent) review, a decision is made within [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours] of receiving [the complete request / all required clinical information]. This compares with [standard decision timeframe] for a standard (non-urgent) request.

Who can ask for expedited review: [who may request expedited review, e.g., the prescriber, the member, or an authorized representative].

When a request qualifies: A request is reviewed on an expedited basis when [criteria for expedited review, e.g., the prescriber indicates that waiting for a standard decision could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health, or ability to regain maximum function].

How to request it: [how to submit or flag an expedited request, e.g., phone, fax, or electronic PA portal, plus any required attestation].

What happens if the request does not qualify: [process if the request is not accepted as expedited, e.g., it is moved to the standard timeframe and the member/prescriber is notified within [notification timeframe]].

If more information is needed: [whether the clock pauses or extends when additional information is requested, and any allowed extension period].

How the decision is communicated: The prescriber and member are notified by [notification method(s)] within [notification timeframe].

If no decision is made in time: [what happens if the timeframe is missed, if defined by plan or regulation].

If the request is denied: [appeal options, including expedited appeal and its timeframe].

Note: Timeframes may differ by plan type: [plan-specific differences, e.g., Commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid, or state-regulated plans].

author_checklist: Confirm the expedited prior authorization decision timeframe and its unit (hours or business/calendar days).
Confirm when the timeframe starts: on receipt of the request, or on receipt of complete clinical information.
Confirm the standard (non-expedited) decision timeframe for comparison.
Confirm who may request expedited review and the eligibility criteria, including any prescriber attestation.
Confirm the submission channels for expedited requests.
Confirm the process and notification when a request is downgraded to standard review.
Confirm the rules for requesting additional information, including any extensions or clock pauses.
Confirm the notification method and timing for prescribers and members.
Confirm the consequence if the decision timeframe is missed.
Confirm expedited appeal options and timeframes after a denial.
Confirm whether timeframes vary by line of business or state regulation, and list each variation.
Verify alignment with current regulatory requirements (e.g., CMS, state law) and the plan contract.
Have the Pharmacy policy owner and Compliance review before approval.
